headline: Bangladesh Bank cuts policy rate to 9.50% to boost investment
summary: The central bank reduced the repo rate by 50 basis points after 21 months, aiming to stimulate economic growth and job creation.
details: Bangladesh Bank has reduced its policy rate, also known as the repo rate, from 10% to 9.50%. The decision was made during a Monetary Policy Committee meeting on Thursday, July 30.
caption:
After 21 months, Bangladesh Bank has finally cut the policy rate to 9.50% to spark investment and job creation.

Bangladesh Bank has reduced its policy rate, also known as the repo rate, from 10% to 9.50%. The decision was made during a Monetary Policy Committee meeting on Thursday, July 30.

headline_marked: Gold prices [[rise again in Bangladesh]] by 2,216 BDT per bhori
headline: Gold prices rise again in Bangladesh by 2,216 BDT per bhori
summary: The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) has increased the price of 22-carat gold to 223,074 BDT per bhori, citing a rise in local pure gold prices.
details: The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) has increased the price of gold in the local market after a three-day gap. The price of 22-carat gold, including VAT, has been set at 223,074 BDT per bhori, an increase of 2,216 BDT.

According to a notice issued by BAJUS on Friday morning, the new prices became effective from 10:00 AM today. The association stated that the price hike was driven by the increase in the price of pure gold in the local market.
Under the new pricing, 21-carat gold is priced at 213,430 BDT per bhori, 18-carat gold at 182,950 BDT, and traditional method gold at 149,474 BDT per bhori.
BAJUS noted that these prices will remain in effect until further notice. While the price of gold is fixed, additional wages based on the jewelry design will be applicable to customers.
VAT is already included in the selling price of gold and silver jewelry, so jewelers are instructed not to collect VAT separately from customers.
This latest adjustment comes after a price drop on July 28, where 22-carat gold was reduced to 220,857 BDT per bhori. The current hike represents a reversal of that previous decrease.
So far this year, gold prices in the local market have been adjusted 97 times. Out of these, prices have increased 47 times, decreased 49 times, and one adjustment was for VAT.
The association ensures that previous rules regarding the exchange and purchase of jewelry, excluding specific VAT, wages, and stones, will remain unchanged.
caption:
Gold prices in Bangladesh just jumped again. 22-carat gold now costs 223,074 BDT per bhori.

The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) has increased the price of gold in the local market after a three-day gap. The price of 22-carat gold, including VAT, has been set at 223,074 BDT per bhori, an increase of 2,216 BDT.

According to a notice issued by BAJUS on Friday morning, the new prices became effective from 10:00 AM today. The association stated that the price hike was driven by the increase in the price of pure gold in the local market.

Under the new pricing, 21-carat gold is priced at 213,430 BDT per bhori, 18-carat gold at 182,950 BDT, and traditional method gold at 149,474 BDT per bhori.

BAJUS noted that these prices will remain in effect until further notice. While the price of gold is fixed, additional wages based on the jewelry design will be applicable to customers.

VAT is already included in the selling price of gold and silver jewelry, so jewelers are instructed not to collect VAT separately from customers.

This latest adjustment comes after a price drop on July 28, where 22-carat gold was reduced to 220,857 BDT per bhori. The current hike represents a reversal of that previous decrease.

So far this year, gold prices in the local market have been adjusted 97 times. Out of these, prices have increased 47 times, decreased 49 times, and one adjustment was for VAT.

The association ensures that previous rules regarding the exchange and purchase of jewelry, excluding specific VAT, wages, and stones, will remain unchanged.
